method.label: Match a double angle to a complement

annotationRationale: Right-triangle ratios and the sine double-angle formula identify sin(2α) with cos β. The supplied math:reciprocal-trig-identities node explicitly includes sin(2t)=2sin(t)cos(t). The complementary-angle identity and acute-angle monotonicity then identify the angles.
sourceMethod: Followed the official first solution using the sine double-angle formula, adding the angle-range justification needed to infer equality of angles from equality of their sines.

review.mathCheck: The shortest-side angles give sin α = 3/5, cos α = 4/5, and cos β = 24/25. Hence sin(2α) = sin(π/2−β). Both arguments lie strictly between 0 and π/2, where sine is injective, so β = π/2−2α, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA solution 10's first approach, p.5: sine doubling followed by complementary-angle identification. The explicit acute-range justification also agrees with the p.6 diagram.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed nodes cover ratios, sine doubling, and the complementary identity. Sine monotonicity appropriately supports branch selection. No full-domain identity derivation is claimed.
